critic_on_address_country.reason: Enum map literal key matching (upper() then map_enum) fails on 'Australia.' (trailing period), emitting the literal placeholder '__PASSTHROUGH__' instead of 'AU'. Output '__PASSTHROUGH__' observed in holdout for Country 'Australia.' — the placeholder leaked into the data and is not a country. Should strip punctuation and default to 'AU'.

Mapping rationale claims ~89% present and non-AU values (e.g. Singapore) pass through as uppercase text; address.country has default AU but is a plain string, so passthrough is tolerable — but the observed placeholder bug above takes precedence; needs the enum default fixed.

critic_summary: Most mappings are semantically sound: legal_name, abn, website, date_registered, address components and state all match their canonical targets, and date order (DD/MM) is correct. The one real defect is address.country: the enum map only recognises 'AUSTRALIA'/'AU'/'AUS' literally after upper(), so a punctuated value 'Australia.' leaves the placeholder '__PASSTHROUGH__' in output instead of 'AU' — observed in a holdout record. Secondary quality issues: locality/full retain trailing commas (e.g. 'Salisbury Plain,'), and no entity_type/acn/industry_code/status are mapped (correctly, absent source columns). No legal-name-as-trading-name or identifier-as-name confusions found. Trading_name untested (all null) but target is right.
